transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Robbins (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sanjay Patel (CISO - Hawthorne), Erin Walsh (Dir Eng), Miguel Torres (Cloud Architect)

Summary: Quick SOC 2 / ISO posture review focused on evidence access, controls mapping, and technical integration points for encryption and VPC options.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, thanks for joining; glad we could get this on the calendar to run through our SOC 2 and ISO posture and how it ties to Hawthorne's clinical workloads.
[00:18] Sanjay: Thanks Maya. We're trying to get comfortable with the assurance artifacts early — procurement asked for SOC 2 Type II and an ISO scope. Also need to know what evidence we can pull for our auditors.
[00:32] Maya: Absolutely. Liam will go through the trust center access and the kinds of artifacts we provide; I'll cover procurement next steps.
[00:40] Liam: Hi all. We host the SOC 2 Type II report for Redwood services, we also have an ISO 27001 certificate; both are available via our Trust Center. I'll drop links after the call. For evidence we provide a controls mapping CSV that maps customer control IDs to Redwood control artifacts.
[00:58] Erin: Quick question — is the SOC 2 scope the hosted API only or does it include Dedicated and Private?
[01:10] Liam: Good question. Our SOC 2 Type II covers the hosted Redwood API and core control plane. For Dedicated and Private deployments we have controls that apply, and we provide additional guidance and attestation language; the ISO scope similarly covers the platform — but private deployments do need a slightly different set of evidence since networking and customer-managed infra are in scope on your side.
[01:34] Miguel: So for Private we need to know what evidence Redwood supplies vs what we have to collect — e.g., KMS integration logs, HSM config, network segmentation evidence.
[01:44] Liam: Right. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. We can provide logs of key use from our side and integration steps, but the actual config and HSM attestations depend on customer-managed KMS. We'll map that in the controls spreadsheet.
[02:02] Sanjay: Data residency — are there options to keep all PHI in our region? We need EU and US boundaries for different tenants.
[02:12] Liam: Yes, we support routing and region pinning. For Hosted we have regionally isolated clusters; for Dedicated and Private you can ensure everything is within a chosen region. We'll include specific region SLAs in the Dedicated appendix.
[02:30] Erin: Audit logs — we need immutable logs with at least two years retention and proof of tamper-evidence for clinical audits. What do you provide?
[02:40] Liam: We provide per-request audit logs including request metadata, identity, model and route, timestamps, and token counts. Logs are writable to your S3 or can be stored in our log retention for configurable retention windows. Tamper-evidence is supported via write-once retention policies and signed log exports; we'll include details and sample exports.
[03:00] Sanjay: How soon can we get a sample export to validate with our auditors?
[03:06] Liam: I can generate a redacted sample export and controls mapping by Friday, 2026-03-12.
[03:12] Miguel: Network-wise we prefer VPC peering or private link. Anything special we should test?
[03:18] Liam: We support VPC peering and private link for Dedicated/Private. We recommend a short connectivity test — small egress check and a TLS handshake test — we can schedule that for the week of 2026-03-22.
[03:32] Erin: SSO — we use Okta, SAML 2.0. Support for RBAC? Group sync?
[03:40] Maya: Yes, we have SAML SSO integrations with Okta and SCIM-based provisioning. RBAC is role-based teams with granular permissions — we can sync groups via SCIM.
[03:50] Sanjay: Can we get a mapping of roles to evidentiary artifacts? Like who can access logs, who can manage keys.
[03:58] Liam: We'll include that in the controls mapping doc — role to permission mapping and associated logs.
[04:06] Miguel: Encryption at rest — what KMS options? We need to see HSM backed keys and customer KMS control.
[04:14] Liam: You can use customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) with keys that we reference. For HSM-backed keys, if you provide an external HSM or KMS with HSM backing, we integrate. We'll document the crypto flow and provide ledgered key-use logs.
[04:30] Erin: Any gotchas around tokenization or PII redaction? We will tokenize clinical IDs before sending, but want to know typical downstream logs contain.
[04:40] Liam: Logs contain request metadata but we do not persist full request payloads by default for hosted; persistence and retention depend on your config. For Dedicated/Private you control retention. We'll show the default retention policy in Trust Center.
[04:58] Sanjay: Who signs the BAA — do you offer HIPAA BAA for clinical data?
[05:06] Maya: Yes, we do offer a BAA for customers handling PHI. We'll have legal send a draft and include BAA language in the contract appendix.
[05:16] Miguel: For controls mapping — our auditors expect crosswalk to NIST/ISO control IDs. Do you have templates?
[05:24] Liam: We maintain mapping templates to SOC 2 criteria, ISO 27001 Annex A, and NIST. We'll share a CSV that has Redwood control ID, control description, artifact link, and suggested customer evidence.
[05:40] Erin: Is the Trust Center self-serve or do we need Redwood to request access?
[05:46] Liam: You can self-request access; we also grant access through the AE. I'll send the Trust Center link and a short onboarding guide. (link: https://redwood.ai/trust-center)
[06:00] Sanjay: About technical evidence — can we get a live walkthrough of the log format? Maybe a short session for our auditors?
[06:08] Maya: Yes — we can do a short session; probably SE-led. We'll plan that after we share the sample export.
[06:16] Miguel: One more question on isolation — if we go Dedicated, do we get dedicated GPU pools and separate tenancy at the network level?
[06:24] Liam: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, network isolation, and tenant separation at the runtime. We'll share the Dedicated security appendix which lists isolation controls and SLA numbers.
[06:36] Erin: Any encryption in transit specifics? Do you support mTLS between service components?
[06:42] Liam: TLS 1.2+ for all endpoints; mTLS for private link and peering options is available for Dedicated/Private. We'll include cipher suites and handshake logs in the security appendix.
[06:56] Sanjay: Ok, procurement will expect to see SOC 2 Type II, ISO cert, BAA, and a controls mapping that aligns to our auditor template. Also I'd like evidence around incident response timelines and last pen test summary.
[07:14] Liam: We have incident response runbooks, average MTTD/MTTR metrics in the Trust Center, and a recent penetration test executive summary we can share; full reports are under NDA but we can share redacted summaries.
[07:32] Erin: Can we get RBAC examples? Like admin, auditor, operator roles and what they can see.
[07:40] Liam: Yes — the mapping doc includes role examples and the permission matrix.
[07:46] Maya: I'll recap — SE will share SOC 2 Type II and controls mapping by 3/12; AE to send Trust Center link, contract/BAA next steps; customer to share auditor template and stakeholders. We'll schedule VPC test week of 3/22 and a short auditor walkthrough once they review sample logs.
[08:06] Sanjay: Sounds good. Also want to note — competitors were asking if you support per-tenant encryption keys, how are you positioned?
[08:16] Liam: We support per-tenant keys via customer-managed KMS; some competitors only provide platform keys. We'll include implementation notes.
[08:24] Miguel: For the connectivity test please include a checklist of endpoints and IP ranges.
[08:30] Liam: We'll send that with the connectivity invite.
[08:36] Erin: Any compliance add-ons like extended log retention or FIPS 140 modules?
[08:44] Liam: We offer extended retention as an add-on and FIPS/HSM-backed key options depending on cloud provider. We'll include those in the price appendix.
[08:54] Sanjay: Great. That's all from me.
[08:58] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[09:02] Miguel: Appreciate it.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels were auto-assigned; small transcription errors present (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated").

References mentioned: Trust Center - https://redwood.ai/trust-center; SOC 2 Type II (to be shared: link/file), Dedicated security appendix (to be attached by SE).

Recap / Next Steps: 1) Liam to share SOC 2 Type II report and controls mapping CSV by 2026-03-12. 2) Maya to circulate trust-center link and procurement next steps by 2026-03-11. 3) Miguel to share auditor contacts and evidence template by 2026-03-15. 4) VPC connectivity test scheduled week of 2026-03-22 (TBD exact day).

End of transcript.
